title: Fermy Lab: Portfolio | Studio 1947
description: Brand identity, packaging and UI for Fermy Lab, a fermented food brand that joins traditional Indian cooking wisdom with modern design.
ogDescription: Brand identity, packaging and a UI system for Fermy Lab, a fermented food brand that joins traditional Indian cooking wisdom with modern design.

hero.alt: Fermy Lab horizontal logo lockup: the wordmark in deep green and golden ochre above a row of ingredient icons

body: When food founders and consumer brands look for a creative agency, they aren't just after attractive graphics. They want a working commercial system: one that earns trust on a grocery shelf, gets noticed on delivery apps, and adapts smoothly as the company grows.
This case study shows how we turned the founding values of Fermy Lab into a polished, scalable identity system built for real business growth.

sections.heading: Context & The Challenge
sections.label: The Mission
body: Fermy Lab is a food brand that makes premium products using slow, natural fermentation. It joins traditional Indian cooking wisdom with proven techniques from cultures around the world. The aim is food that is healthy, enjoyable and kind to the environment, with no artificial preservation shortcuts.

sections.label: The Creative Challenge
body: The brand sits at a crossroads: deep tradition and modern thinking, local roots and global ideas, natural patience and scientific rigour. To express that balance, we anchored the branding in the idea of “calm confidence”. The style is clean and systematic, yet warm and handcrafted. It shows customers that slow food can be professional, clean and world-class.

sections.heading: Parent-Brand Architecture
body: To save the client design costs later, we built a "parent-child" visual system with room to grow:

media.alt: Parent-brand architecture diagram: the Fermy Lab master mark sitting above two product tracks, Breads and Condiments, each with its own product line labelling

body: Fermy Lab is the master identity. Under it, the brand launches with two product tracks: Breads and Condiments. Each item carries its own product line labelling, while the master mark stays prominent across everything. So the business can launch new items straight away without paying for a full brand redesign.

sections.heading: Color & Typography Systems
sections.label: The Palette
body: The colour identity uses a high-contrast pairing made to stand out on store shelves:

swatches.name: Deep Green
swatches.note: Stands for natural fermentation cycles, organic balance, and safety and trust.

swatches.name: Golden Ochre
swatches.note: Suggests warm oven-baked goodness, rich raw nourishment, and hand-crafted cooking skill.

cards.title: Space Grotesk
cards.body:
Usage
Headlines, packaging titles and technical system signage.

The Strategy
Space Grotesk brings a clean, disciplined geometric frame that echoes the “Lab” in the brand name. It stays sharp on printed packaging and on screens. And because it is free in the open-source Google Fonts library, marketing teams anywhere can build matching assets without licensing trouble.

cards.title: Just Sans
cards.body:
Usage
Brand stories, back-of-label explanations and detailed ingredient lists.

The Strategy
To balance the technical look of the primary font, we paired it with Just Sans. It adds a friendly, modernist warmth and clear geometric shapes. Health labels and brand stories stay approachable and easy for customers to scan.

sections.heading: The Logo Usage & Visual Governance
body: To keep the logo consistent across very different labels and screens, we gathered every configuration, safety guideline and prohibition into a single technical standard.

media.alt: Overview of the Fermy Lab logo usage system: the approved lockup configurations gathered into one technical standard

sections.label: The Master Badge Lockup
body: This is the main seal of quality. It brings the brand name, core ingredients and service taglines together in a circular stamp. An illustrated wreath shows real ingredients: twisted challah bread, garlic bulbs, star anise, cloves and chillies.

media.alt: The master badge lockup: a circular Fermy Lab stamp ringed by an illustrated wreath of challah bread, garlic, star anise, cloves and chilis

sections.label: The Horizontal Lockup
body: Made for tight spaces where the logo still needs to be seen. This inline version sets the wordmark directly above a simple row of ingredient icons.

media.alt: The horizontal lockup: the Fermy Lab wordmark set inline above a streamlined row of ingredient icons for tight spaces

sections.label: Responsive Favicons
body: Simple, high-contrast circular badges that pick out a single icon, such as the mini bread loaf or a clove. They keep the identity sharp on tiny screens.

media.alt: Responsive favicon set: simplified circular badges each isolating one icon, such as the bread loaf or a clove, for micro-screen legibility

sections.label: The 1-Challah Clearspace Rule
body: So the master mark is never crowded by copy or layout edges, it always gets a minimum safety border. That breathing room is exactly one "1 Challah distance", taken from the height of the twisted bread illustration inside the badge.

media.alt: Clearspace diagram: the master badge surrounded by a minimum safety border measured as one challah loaf height on every side

sections.label: Partner Co-Branding Safety Margin
body: When the logo sits next to distribution partners or established institutions (for example, a historic name like Amul), the system keeps a strict 1-Challah safety margin to protect FermyLab's own authority.
The FermyLab logo isn't just a symbol, it's a statement. Keep it clear, crisp, and confidently placed.

media.alt: Co-branding diagram: the Fermy Lab mark locked up beside a partner logo with the mandated 1-Challah safety perimeter between them

sections.heading: Absolute Production Prohibitions
body: To remove any guesswork for printers or developers, we wrote a clear checklist of what not to do. Production must never make the following changes:

media.alt: Violation matrix: a checklist of prohibited treatments of the Fermy Lab mark, such as recolouring, stretching and rotating it

sections.heading: Putting the System to Work
body: To show how the identity wins customers in physical shops and on digital platforms, we applied the brand assets across the key commercial touchpoints

sections.label: Physical Retail Packaging
body: Clean badge labels wrap neatly around slow-aged condiment jars. The result is elegant and editorial, and it stands out on a busy retail shelf.

media.alt: Retail packaging: slow-aged condiment jars wrapped in clean Fermy Lab badge labels

body: Clean badge labels wrap neatly around slow-aged condiment jars. The result is elegant and editorial, and it stands out on a busy retail shelf.

media.alt: The digital flagship: Fermy Lab e-commerce storefront screens carrying the identity through product and checkout pages

sections.label: Delivery App Optimization
body: We tuned the brand assets for dark-mode delivery apps on phones. When a customer is scrolling quickly through restaurant options, FermyLab's product cards, details and icons stay crisp and readable.

media.alt: Delivery app listings: Fermy Lab product cards, metadata and icons tuned for dark-mode smartphone food-delivery interfaces

sections.label: Out-of-Home Highway Billboards
body: Big highway billboards pair huge food photography with a few words ("No shortcuts. Just fermentation.") to build mainstream awareness fast.

media.alt: Highway billboard: oversized food photography paired with the minimal line "No shortcuts. Just fermentation."

sections.heading: Commercial Value Summary
body: Instead of a loose set of graphic files, we gave Fermy Lab a disciplined, complete brand toolkit. The business is ready to stand out on shelves, look sharp on screens, and launch new sub-brands with confidence and no added design debt.
